headline: Frost and patchy fog are likely early Monday, then mostly dry and warmer midweek, with cooler, rainier weather possible by Saturday.
summary: As of Sunday evening, skies were clear and winds light, so temperatures should drop quickly overnight. A Frost Advisory runs from midnight tonight to 8 AM Monday for much of the Puget Sound area from south of Seattle southward, plus Hood Canal and the North Coast. Frost ends the growing season in these areas. Patchy fog is possible early Monday, mainly in the southern interior and valleys. If temperatures reach freezing, it could be freezing fog, but forecasters are unsure how cold it will get. Highs Monday should climb a bit, with most inland areas topping 60 degrees. More clouds arrive Monday night as a weak atmospheric river (a narrow stream of moisture) aims at British Columbia. Most of its rain should stay north of the border, though some may clip the northwestern Olympic Peninsula and the northern interior on Tuesday. The extra clouds may limit frost and fog early Tuesday. Wednesday looks mostly dry for most of the region, with the best rain chances again on the Olympic Peninsula and northern interior, though the moisture's path may shift. An upper-level ridge (a zone of high pressure aloft that brings warm, dry weather) builds Thursday and Friday, and warming may begin as early as Wednesday. Highs should reach the upper 60s to lower 70s by Friday, and some Cascade valleys, including the Highway 12 corridor, may hit the upper 70s. Forecasters do not expect daily records. By Saturday the ridge shifts well to the east and a trough (a dip in the jet stream) develops over the Pacific Northwest, which will likely bring rain chances and cooler temperatures. Weekend details remain uncertain.
changes: The early-morning and morning discussions called for Friday highs in the mid 60s to mid 70s and a possible warm front bringing rain Friday night into Saturday. By evening, Friday highs were given as upper 60s to lower 70s, and Saturday was described as a trough bringing likely rain chances and cooler temperatures.
